ADJOURNED EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  December 18, 2017

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ called the meeting to order, the time being 6:01 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Velveth Schmitz
Susan Brtis
Carol Dean-Porter
Patricia Harik*
Bill Kemp
Lou Persichina
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano**
*Arrived at 6:57 p.m.
**Arrived at 6:37 p.m.

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF OCTOBER 23, 2017
MEMBER DEAN-PORTER moved, seconded by MEMBER KEMP

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE OCTOBER 23, 2017 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
Candice Ham, 26802 Rolling Hills Road, RHE notified the Equestrian Committee that she was
injured on the Palamino Trail by tripping over an exposed manhole cover. CHAIRMAN
SCHMITZ asked the Community Services Director to find out whose responsibility it is when
utility easements coincide with bridle/hiking trail easements and issues like this arise. In
addition, she asked that the City’s Maintenance Division staff survey all the trail areas that
have manhole covers. MEMBER KEMP reported there was also a similar situation on the
Rolling Hills Road Trail near west Lariat Lane.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
DECEMBER 18, 2017  1
 Richard Oldroyd, 40 Ranchview Road, RHE reported that wind was blowing trash out of an
uncovered and overfilled recycle bin at the Rolling Hills United Methodist Church and blowing
onto the adjacent bridle/hiking trail. The Community Services Director indicated that he would
have the City’s Code Enforcement staff meet with the Church and have the City’s
Maintenance Division staff remove the litter from this trail. In response to another inquiry from
Mr. Oldroyd, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ stated that the City was not aware Seahorse Riding
Club’s interest to have their property re-zoned.

Ely Arencibia, 63 Buckskin Lane, RHE inquired whether the City had an equine emergency
response plan. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ responded that there a plan was available on the
City’s website, along with additional emergency preparedness and response information.

SELECT EQUESTRIAN COMMUNITY REPRESENTATIVE FOR CALIFORNIA WATER
SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT MONTHLY UPDATE MEETINGS
The Community Services Director reported that California Water Service Company was
seeking an equestrian community member to attend a monthly meeting to receive updates
about the upcoming Water Reliability Project. He noted that the representative could be an
Equestrian Committee Member, City Council Member, City staff, or a member of the local
equestrian community.

Nancy Wildman, 34 Pony Lane, RHE attended the first update meeting on behalf of the City
and CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ asked her to provide the Committee information about the
meeting. Ms. Wildman stated that she had recently become a paid consultant for California
Water Service Company and should not continue as the City’s equestrian community
representative. She stated that the first update meeting was held during a free lunch at Good
Stuff Restaurant, where California Water Service Company project staff gave an overview of
the project and answered questions from the attendees. Ms. Wildman noted that while this
company is trying hard to be as least disruptive as possible with the Water Liability Project,
they acknowledge that they will not be able to please everyone. In response to CHAIRMAN
SCHMITZ’S inquiry, Ms. Wildman stated that California Water Service Company staff
indicated that the average water bill will increase by approximately $30 per month for most
Peninsula residents upon completion of the replacement of the 60 year old main water line.

MEMBER SHINN volunteered to be the Equestrian Committee representative and inquired
whether there could be an alternate representative. The Committee agreed and she
recommended that MEMBER SILVANO be the alternate and MEMBER BRTIS volunteered to
be the second alternate, if needed. The Community Services Director stated that he would
notify California Water Service Company of the City’s equestrian community representatives.

HORSES FOR MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE – MAY 5, 2018
The Community Services Director reported that he had exhausted every horse rental vendor
lead that he had received for this region and had not been able to secure any horses for the
City Council and invited elected officials who regularly rode in the event. He stated that he
had written a letter to Jim Moore in regards to a possibility that he knew a horse rental vendor

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
DECEMBER 18, 2017  2
 in the Victorville area. Audience member, Nancy Wildman, indicated that the horse rental firm
in Victorville was likely Graham Brothers. The Community Services Director thanked Ms.
Wildman for this information and noted to the Committee and audience members that anyone
with a horse that could be loaned to the City for this event would be of great assistance.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ reminded the Equestrian Committee and audience members that City
Council was very disappointed about the lack of interest by the equestrian community last
year and that if this occurred again for the 2018 the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride, the event would
likely be permanently cancelled. The Community Services Director indicated that he would
put the recommendations developed by the Equestrian Committee at the May 30, 2017
meeting to improve participation in the 2018 Ride event on the January 23, 2018 meeting
agenda for the Committee’s review.

EQUESTRIAN/PEDESTRIAN STREET CROSSINGS PROJECT UPDATE
The Community Services Director reported that the Assistant City Manager indicated that
there were several delays for this project’s completion, including project supplies back-orders
and equipment delivered which could not be connected to the installed equipment. It was
hoped that the crossing lights would be working this week, except that it was discovered there
was an electrical issue which popped all the new light bulbs. The electrical issue has been
corrected and new bulbs have been ordered and expected to be installed soon.

INCREASING ATTENDANCE AND PARTICIPATION  AT  CITY  CELEBRATION
EQUESTRIAN EVENTS AND ACTIVITIES
The Community Services Director reviewed the City Celebration Debriefing Minutes from the
Joint Meeting of City Council and the Park and Activities Commission on November 8, 2017
specifically related to the equestrian events and activities. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ noted that
she observed no spectators watching the equestrian events in Howlett Park’s arenas despite
having more signage at the event. The Community Services Director also noted that high
school volunteers were also handing out Schedules of Events in the parking areas resulting in
more AYSO Soccer families participating in the event this year.

Audience member Ely Arencibia reported that her family arrived about 1:00 p.m. and it
seemed that the equestrian events were already over. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ informed Ms.
Arencibia that the event schedule was shortened due to the lack of afternoon event patrons
the past few years and that the City collaborated with the Remember the Music Festival this
year to provide music for attendees.

Audience Member Pam Schachter believes that Jim Moore’s past suggestion to have
someone walking around with a portable public address system telling park patrons the
schedule of upcoming activities should be reconsidered. MEMBER SHINN suggested that
the event should start later in the morning around 10:30 a.m. and to encourage City officials
and local horse trainers to attend the equestrian events.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
DECEMBER 18, 2017  3
 In response to CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ’S inquiry, audience member, Kelly Yates suggested
that equestrian demonstrations, such as the Junior Drill Team, could be offered during the
afternoon portion of the event. In addition, the demonstration horses could be part of a Horse
Breeds Exhibition in the barn in the morning and early afternoon hours.

MEMBER SHINN recommended that hay and water be provided at the barn as an incentive
for local equestrians to bring their horses to Ernie Howlett Park’s equestrian center. She also
felt that the Pony Rides and Petting Zoo could be moved into the rectangular warm-up arena
to avoid any potential conflicts with young children around the barn area. It was also
suggested that the Poker Ride check-in be placed near the barn area.

Audience member, Pam Schachter, stated that more assistance is needed from the City’s
Maintenance Division staff, specifically Mike Goldsmith, Maintenance Supervisor for the
equestrian activities and demonstrations to go smoothly. The Community Services Director
requested that a list of specific tasks that need to occur as specific times should be submitted
to Mike Goldsmith prior to the event. In addition, Ms. Schachter believes that more walkie-
talkies are needed.

Audience member, Kelly Yates, said that she spoke to Susie Lytle prior to the meeting who
was interested in coordinating a Parade of Breeds demonstration next year. Ms. Yates also
felt that the Poker Ride riders’ arrival time at the park needed to be coordinated for maximum
participation in the various equestrian activities and events that would occur in Howlett Park’s
equestrian center. She also described a number of Horse Happenings event demonstrations
that were successful a few years ago, including Veterinarian workshops and horse trainer
demonstrations.

MEMBER SHINN believes that advance publicity is key to attract local equestrians to the City
Celebration event through sources such as the PVPHA Dispatch newsletter, equestrian
events flyers distributed to area stores, and social media. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ inquired
whether the City could redistribute the PVPHA Dispatch newsletter through its social media or
have a link on the City’s website and Nancy Wildman, PVPHA Dispatch editor, indicated that
this would be welcomed.

Kelly Yates stated that requiring event patrons to park across the street is a deterrent to
attending the City Celebration. MEMBER PERSICHINA suggested that a hayride be set up
that would pick-up and drop-off riders in Howlett Park’s equestrian area to encourage viewing
of the equestrian demonstrations and activities.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ noted that there was a Park and Activities Commission about to start
in the Council Chambers, and therefore, the meeting must conclude with the City Celebration
discussion continuing at the January 23, 2018 Equestrian Committee meeting. She also
stated that this may be her last meeting as Chairman, as she had chaired the Equestrian
Committee for the past two years and that the new Mayor typically rotates Committee
Chairmanships every few years. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ thanked the Committee Members for
their dedication and interest in preserving and enhancing the equestrian heritage of the City.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
DECEMBER 18, 2017  4
 EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
There were no issues to report since the October 23, 2017 Equestrian Committee meeting.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
  None.
B.  SEAHORSE RIDING CLUB SOLD
  MEMBER SHINN reported that Seahorse Riding Club had been sold and requested
  that this item be placed on the January 23, 2018 Committee Meeting agenda.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE - Monthly
B.  2018 MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE PARTICIPATION RECOMMENDATIONS –
  January 23, 2018
C.  SEAHORSE RIDING CLUB SALE – January 23, 2018
D.  LICENSED HORSE TRAINER BACKGROUND CHECKS – January 23, 2018
E.  ANNUAL LICENSED HORSE TRAINERS MEETING – February 26, 2018 at 6:00pm
  (prior to Equestrian Committee meeting)

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by MEMBER DEAN-PORTER

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 6:58 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
